conditions.label: Anemia in neoplastic disease
conditions.note: anemia of chronic disease, Hgb 9.2 in July 2024

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Daughter with her. Made it to the graduation in October in the wheelchair, stayed for the whole ceremony, rested two days after. Very happy she went.
July oncology note finally came in October: Hgb 9.2, Ca 10.5, albumin 3.0, no med changes. Updating the list from it.
Since then: tired, naps daily. Pain unchanged on the morphine. Eating small meals with supplement drinks. Bowels ok.

Exam: cachectic, in wheelchair. Pale conjunctivae. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Diffuse bony tenderness. No edema.

A/P
1. Anemia of chronic disease (neoplastic) - added. Oncology following counts with treatment.
2. Low albumin - added; nutrition as above.
3. Metastatic breast ca, cancer pain, OIC, cachexia/sarcopenia - per oncology, regimen unchanged.
4. Vit D deficiency/osteomalacia - on weekly D and calcium. CMP today.
RTC April AWV.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count is low but about where oncology has been seeing it. Calcium and kidney tests are fine. No changes.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Pt with daughter; husband waited in the car.
Now needs help with bathing and dressing most days; husband helps mornings, daughter evenings and weekends and handles the pill box and all appointments. Wheelchair outside the house.
PHQ-2 2. Low mood on bad pain days, enjoys her grandchildren's visits. Not interested in counseling.
Cognition intact.
Advance care: proxy daughter. She brought up on her own that if treatment stops working she would rather be comfortable at home than in a hospital. Documented; family meeting offered whenever she wants it.

Exam: cachectic. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Bony tenderness unchanged.

Plan: no screening indicated. Vaccines current. Continue oncology-directed care. RTC 3-4 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Medical oncology visit, July 2025
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - CLINIC NOTE
Date of service: 07/21/2025

Ms. Zhang is a 68-year-old with stage IV invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast with osseous metastases, accompanied today by her daughter. She had periods of response early on, but the disease has now progressed. Over three years she has received several lines of chemotherapy and targeted therapy. She reports worsening fatigue and poor appetite, and her pain is not well controlled on her oral opioid regimen. She tells us she would like to put her quality of life first rather than continue with aggressive treatment.

Her daughter, who manages her medications and care, says she is overwhelmed by the amount she is handling.

Medications: morphine sulfate ER 30 mg q12h; morphine sulfate IR 15 mg q4h prn breakthrough pain; cholecalciferol 50,000 units weekly; calcium carbonate 600 mg tid with meals; senna 8.6 mg bid; docusate 100 mg bid; prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn nausea; mirtazapine 15 mg qhs.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Vitals stable. Exam: cachectic, seated in a wheelchair. Lungs clear.

Labs: hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, calcium 10.2 mg/dL, albumin 3.0 g/dL, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL.

Assessment/Plan: Progressive metastatic breast cancer. Treatment options and her priorities discussed at length; she will think about next steps with her family. Medications unchanged today. We encourage involving her primary care physician in planning for support at home.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Oncology note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Oncology note in. Progression, pt leaning toward quality-of-life focus, daughter overwhelmed. Asked front desk to get her in within 2 weeks with daughter and husband if possible.

orders.reason: homebound with metastatic cancer, caregiver strain

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - support at home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Long visit, pt with daughter; husband joined by phone.
Oncology note 7/21 reviewed: disease progressing, Hgb 9.8, Ca 10.2, albumin 3.0, Cr 1.2. Pt reiterates she wants to focus on how she feels and is weighing whether to continue treatment.
Daughter: works part time, sets up all meds, drives to every appointment, up most nights checking on her mother. Says she is at the end of her rope. Husband does meals and daytime help but has trouble getting her on and off the toilet.
Pt: tired, wants to stay home. Pain worse some evenings despite IR doses; she will raise doses with oncology, who prescribe.

Exam: cachectic, in wheelchair. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Diffuse bony tenderness.

A/P
1. Caregiver strain / not enough support at home - home health referral for nursing (med management, pain review) and aide for bathing; she qualifies as homebound. Gave daughter caregiver support group info.
2. Progressive metastatic breast cancer - treatment decisions with oncology; offered a family meeting here whenever they are ready.
3. Pain - oncology to adjust; asked daughter to message them this week.
4. Creatinine 1.2, up from her usual - recheck with next labs.
RTC fall.

documents.title: Home health start of care
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home health intake nurse called: start of care visit done 8/25. Skilled nursing weekly, aide 3x/week for bathing. Plan of care faxed for PCP signature. Signed and returned 8/27.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seen in the car at the curb at family's request (transfers hard). High-dose flu and 2025-26 COVID, left arm. Observed 15 min in car with daughter. Fine.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt in her bed at home, daughter holding the tablet.
Home health nurse weekly, aide helps with bathing; daughter says that has made a real difference. Pt still on treatment at the cancer center but tired for days after each one. Pain worse in the evenings. Appetite poor.
No new symptoms reported.
Observed: thin, speaking full sentences, comfortable at rest.

A/P: Progressive metastatic breast cancer with growing needs at home. She and family are talking about whether to stop treatment; oncology visit next month. Repeated offer of a family meeting here. Labs to be drawn before that meeting. Continue current meds per oncology.

documents.title: Family meeting
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (daughter) Hello doctor. Mom saw the cancer doctor last week. The new scans show the cancer has spread more and they said there is no treatment left that will help it. Mom says she is done with treatments anyway. She is more tired, sometimes short of breath, and the pain is harder to control. Can we have that family meeting with you? My father and I will both come. Thank you.

documents.title: RE: Family meeting
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, of course. Front desk will call to set an hour-long time next week. I'm ordering blood work for a couple of days before so we have current numbers. If her breathing gets worse before then, call us right away.

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Drawn in the car per family request, left arm. Tolerated.

orders.reason: progressive stage IV breast cancer, no further disease-directed therapy, patient goals

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Family Meeting - Goals of Care
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
FAMILY MEETING. Present: patient, husband, daughter. 75 minutes, more than half on advance care planning.

Background: R breast IDC 2018, metastatic to bone since 2022, several lines of chemo and targeted therapy plus radiation. Per family, oncology's latest scans show widespread progression and her oncologist has told them nothing further is expected to control the cancer.

Her words: she is tired of treatments and wants the time she has left to be comfortable, at home, with family. She does not want to go back to the hospital unless it's the only way to keep her comfortable.
Symptoms: tired most of the day, short of breath now and then with exertion, pain harder to keep down even with extra IR doses.
Home: lives with husband, who does most of the day-to-day care and admits he can't keep up as her needs grow. Daughter handles meds and appointments. Home health aide 3x/week.

Labs 1/27: Hgb 9.2, Ca 11.4, alk phos 240, Cr 1.8.

Exam: pale, frail, in wheelchair. Breath sounds diminished at both bases. Heart regular. Spine and right hip tender to touch. Calm, engaged in the discussion.

A/P
1. Progressive stage IV breast cancer with bone metastases - patient chooses comfort-focused care. Hospice referral placed today, home hospice. Explained what hospice provides: nurse visits, aide, equipment, 24/7 phone line, medications for comfort.
2. Code status / MOLST - completed and signed with patient: DNR, DNI, comfort-focused treatment, no hospital transfer unless needed for comfort. Copy to family for the refrigerator, copy scanned.
3. Calcium 11.4 - stopping the calcium carbonate and the weekly vitamin D. Not chasing it further given her goals.
4. Pain and breathlessness - hospice team to take over adjusting the morphine; until admission continue current doses and use the IR as prescribed.
5. Caregiver strain - hospice aide hours and respite discussed.
I'll stay involved as her primary physician. Family has the office cell for anything before hospice starts.

documents.title: Hospice admission notice
documents.author: hospice
documents.body:
HOSPICE ADMISSION NOTIFICATION
Patient: Mei Zhang  DOB 03/29/1957
Admission date: 02/04/2026, routine home care.
Terminal diagnosis: malignant neoplasm of breast with secondary malignant neoplasm of bone.
Attending physician of record: primary care physician (as elected by patient).
Code status: DNR/DNI per MOLST dated 01/29/2026.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
Medications on admission: morphine sulfate ER 30 mg q12h, morphine sulfate IR 15 mg q4h prn, senna 8.6 mg bid, docusate 100 mg bid, prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn, mirtazapine 15 mg qhs. Hospice team will adjust the comfort regimen as needed.
RN case manager visits twice weekly; aide visits; chaplain and social work offered and accepted.
Please sign and return the certification of terminal illness.

documents.title: Call with hospice RN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospice RN case manager called with an update. Pt settled, sleeping more, eating little. Pain better since the hospice team adjusted her regimen. Family coping better with the extra aide visits. Certification signed and returned last month. Plan a video visit with family in April.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - home hospice
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video with pt, husband and daughter at home. On home hospice since early February.
Pt in a hospital bed in the living room, by the window. Says she is comfortable most days. Sleeps much of the day, wakes for meals of congee and tea. Breathing ok at rest. Pain manageable, hospice adjusts her medicines. Bowels moving with help.
Family: tired but say hospice has lifted a lot off them; daughter sleeps through most nights now.
Observed: thin, alert, smiling, speaking in short sentences, no distress.

A/P: Metastatic breast cancer on home hospice, comfort goals being met. MOLST in the home. Hospice manages day-to-day medications; our list stays as of the January meeting. Family knows to call hospice first and can reach me anytime. No further visits scheduled; will check in through hospice.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (daughter) Just a note to say Mom is peaceful. Her granddaughter visited this weekend and she was awake for most of it. Thank you for everything.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for writing. I'm glad she had that time with family. Thinking of all of you.

documents.title: Hospice recertification summary
documents.author: hospice
documents.body:
HOSPICE - BENEFIT PERIOD RECERTIFICATION
Patient: Mei Zhang
Continued eligibility: progressive metastatic breast cancer to bone; declining oral intake, increased sleep, dependent for all ADLs.
Comfort goals being met per patient and family. Symptom regimen managed by hospice team.
Please sign and return.

Filed. Signed and returned 6/24 by PCP.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request received for mirtazapine 15 mg qhs (original prescriber oncology). Pt on hospice. Called hospice RN line: they cover her meds and will send the refill. Request declined here with note to pharmacy to contact hospice.

documents.title: Parking placard
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (daughter) Sorry to bother you. Could you fill out the handicap parking form for my father's car so we can take Mom out in the wheelchair on her good days? The old one expired. I can drop off the form.

documents.title: RE: Parking placard
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No bother at all. Drop it at the front desk or upload it here and I'll complete it the same day.
